origin: Proposed synthetic operations, not inspected production source or API guarantees.
unprotectedInterval: ReadIdentity -> ReplaceResource -> optional PublishGeneration -> ApplyEffect. Neither a SQL lock snapshot nor an immutable old-object pin serializes address reassignment with the external effect.

flawedAbstraction.claim: Collapse lock snapshot, metadata read, identity read and external effect into one SQL-protected action.
flawedAbstraction.missingMechanism: No operation covers both external reassignment and effect. The expanded LockWindow actions disclose the omitted interval.

assumptions: Client and backend deaths are distinct. A still-live backend holds its session lock after client death.
A surviving worker reads metadata and performs the effect after both deaths; the dead backend performs no SQL writes.
The address and its current generation change together at replacement; external SQL publication may lag.
Same-store mode removes the cross-system split: replacement updates ownership and authoritative row together, and conditional SQL UPDATE checks that row through the effect.
Service-check mode assumes every resource reassignment and effect is serialized by the resource service.
All variants share the same current-generation safety rule. Immutable-pin mode deliberately still targets the reusable address, not the pinned object.
omissions: Actual lock manager, transaction isolation implementation, reconnect, restart, and real API calls.
Other permutations of death and read order; this fixture isolates one explicit dangerous schedule.

actions.operation: Stop the client; do not terminate the backend or mutate storage.
Read a snapshot of the still-live backend lock. This is not lock acquisition.
Terminate backend and release its session lock independently.
SELECT published generation into a local token.
Observe external generation and pin old object; neither holds a guard on the reusable address.
Reassign address to generation 2. Same-store mode updates the authoritative row in the same operation.
Publish replacement generation to metadata, separately from external replacement.
Unsafe modes use recorded observations. Same-store mode uses UPDATE resource SET effect = value WHERE generation = token. Service-check mode uses conditional resource API.
actions.protectedInterval: Safe modes compare authoritative generation through effect, atomically with respect to all reassignments. No such interval is protected in unsafe modes.

actions.operation: Conditional operation refuses a stale generation and changes no replacement.
